channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: German Public Growing Trust in AfD Party Amidst Government Crisis, Poll Shows
item.description: German public trust in the AfD party is increasing due to dissatisfaction with the government's performance, according to DW. A September "ARD-Deutschlandtrend" poll indicates 84% are unhappy with the federal government. The AfD leads polls at 27%, significantly ahead of the CDU/CSU's 21%.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Islamic Civilization Center Need Distinct International Voice, Says BBC Representative
item.description: Uzbekistan and its Center for Islamic Civilization must develop their own international voice, according to Sergey Stanovkin, BBC Studios' Eurasia commercial representative. The recent International Media Forum in Tashkent, attended by global media, aimed to enhance Uzbekistan's presence in the international information space and showcase its culture and history.

item.title: CCA Tashkent Opens as Central Asia's First Comprehensive Contemporary Art Center
item.description: The Center for Contemporary Art (CCA) Tashkent has opened, featuring exhibition halls, a library, concept store, and educational spaces. Housed in a historic 1912 power station, it's Central Asia's first institution of its kind. Saida Mirziyoyeva highlighted its role in promoting Uzbek artists internationally.

item.title: 83% of Uzbek university graduates employed, new 'Graduate Quality Index' developed
item.description: A study in Uzbekistan reveals that 83% of university graduates are employed. The country has developed a new "Graduate Quality Index" to analyze graduate employment rates, income, and speed of job placement. The findings were published on Daryo.uz.

item.title: Central Asia-China Political Party Dialogue Conference Held in Samarkand
item.description: A conference on the "Role of Political Parties in Strengthening Ties between Central Asian Countries and China" took place in Samarkand. Representatives from political parties of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan, along with a Chinese Communist Party delegation, attended. The dialogue aims to enhance strategic trust and multilateral cooperation between the regions.

item.title: Young Parliamentarians Convene in Samarkand for Global Conference
item.description: Young parliamentarians from 60 countries and 13 international organizations gathered in Samarkand for the XII Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians. The event, initiated by Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, focused on restoring human rights, justice, and dignity in challenging times. Delegates shared experiences and sought common solutions to global issues, emphasizing youth participation.

item.title: World Nomad Games becoming comparable to Olympics, World Cup, says Kyrgyz PM
item.description: Kyrgyzstan handed over the World Nomad Games baton to Russia, with the next edition set for Tatarstan in 2028. Prime Minister Adylbek Kasymaliev stated the games have become a major international cultural and sports movement, comparable to the Olympics and World Cup.

item.title: Uzbekistan U-20 team qualifies for U-20 Asian Cup after defeating Syria
item.description: Uzbekistan's youth national team secured a spot in the U-20 Asian Cup by defeating Syria with a large score. The tournament will be held in China from March 24 to April 10, 2027. Semi-finalists will qualify for the 2027 FIFA U-20 World Cup.

item.title: Uzbekistan Opens Consulate General in Seattle, USA
item.description: Uzbekistan has officially opened its Consulate General in Seattle, Washington, marking the country's first consular presence in the U.S. Pacific Northwest. The new consulate aims to strengthen trade, economic, investment, technological, educational, and humanitarian ties between Uzbekistan and the United States. Its consular district covers Washington, Oregon, Idaho, and Montana.

item.title: 12th Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians Held Successfully in Samarkand
item.description: The 12th Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians, themed 'For Human Rights, Justice, and Dignity in a Complex World,' was successfully held in Samarkand from September 4-6. The event was organized by the Inter-Parliamentary Union.

item.title: New International Airline May Be Established in Uzbekistan in Partnership with Afghanistan
item.description: A new international airline could be established in Uzbekistan in cooperation with Afghanistan. This possibility was discussed in the Fergana region with the head of Kam Air, focusing on available opportunities and necessary infrastructure.

item.title: Criminal Cases in Uzbekistan Courts Increased by 29% in Six Months
item.description: The number of criminal cases heard in Uzbekistan's courts rose by 29% in the first six months of the year. The proportion of grave crimes increased by 18%, and particularly grave crimes by 19%, with the capital seeing the most offenses.

item.title: Uzbek President's Belgrade visit aims to strengthen ties and foster practical cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's upcoming visit to Serbia signifies a new phase in bilateral relations, building on historical Silk Road connections. Both nations express readiness to enhance partnership, with Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić calling the visit a "powerful impetus" for development.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President and Tatarstan Head Discuss Cooperation and World Nomad Games
item.description: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov met with Tatarstan Head Rustam Minnikhanov in Cholpon-Ata. They discussed trade and economic cooperation, with bilateral trade exceeding $182 million last year. Japarov pledged support for the 2028 World Nomad Games in Kazan.

item.title: Uzbek national sentenced to two years for fighting in Ukraine
item.description: A young man from Namangan, Uzbekistan, who joined the Russian army, has been sentenced to two years in prison. During his sentence, military personnel offered prisoners money and Russian citizenship in exchange for participation in the war in Ukraine. Central Asian prisoners who refused were reportedly tortured and placed in solitary confinement.

item.title: Uzbekistan to enhance public safety training with continuous education system
item.description: Uzbekistan is establishing a continuous education system to train professionals in public safety. The initiative aims to equip personnel with modern knowledge and practical skills, aligning with state policy priorities of upholding law, protecting citizen rights, and maintaining social order. A presidential decree emphasizes this transformation.

item.title: Uzbekistan hosts international seminar on green economy and WTO law for legal professionals
item.description: An international seminar on "Green Economy, Energy, and Investment Law within WTO Law" was held in Uzbekistan for legal professionals. Organized with the Konrad Adenauer Foundation, the event focused on WTO principles, Uzbekistan's accession process, green economy, renewable energy, carbon taxes, and foreign investment regulation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces New Opportunities and Legal Guarantees for Entrepreneurs
item.description: A roundtable in Tashkent discussed new opportunities and legal guarantees for entrepreneurs, implementing a presidential decree. Discussions covered support mechanisms, rights protection, and state policy. Significant easing of administrative pressure and financial support measures were announced, including a three-year moratorium on inspections for small businesses.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Adopt Geothermal Heating Technology with Chinese Company
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering implementing building heating technology using geothermal energy in collaboration with a Chinese company. Discussions also covered studying Chinese prefabricated construction standards and technical requirements to enhance efficiency and reduce environmental impact in construction.

item.title: Over 1,500 People Sought Medical Aid During World Nomad Games
item.description: More than 1,500 individuals sought medical assistance during the World Nomad Games, with the majority of cases occurring at the Kyrchen jailoo. Among those treated were 150 foreigners. The games recorded 273 injuries and 101 emergency cases, leading to 75 hospitalizations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Strengthens Inter-Parliamentary Cooperation at Global Conference
item.description: In Samarkand, during the XII Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians, Uzbekistan's Senate Chairperson met with former IPU President Duarte Pacheco and Indian MP Raghav Chadha. Discussions focused on enhancing Uzbekistan's ties with the IPU, parliamentary diplomacy, and bilateral cooperation with Portugal and India.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India Deepen Cooperation in Critical Minerals and Uranium
item.description: Uzbekistan and India are set to deepen their partnership in geological resources, including uranium and critical minerals, according to The Economic Times. A Memorandum of Understanding is being finalized, paving the way for joint exploration and development projects and increased delegation exchanges.

item.title: Youth Dialogue Held at UN Climate Conference in Samarkand
item.description: A dialogue between youth and guests of honor took place at the UN Climate Conference in Samarkand, focusing on youth's role in climate and water resource management. Participants included UN officials and government representatives who discussed climate change risks and the importance of youth engagement in finding solutions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Russia Hold Foreign Ministry Consultations on UN Cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Russia's foreign ministries held consultations on cooperation within the UN framework. The discussions covered a wide range of issues, including Kyrgyzstan's upcoming non-permanent membership in the UN Security Council for 2027-2028. Both sides confirmed similar approaches to international agenda items and explored ways to enhance foreign policy coordination within UN bodies.

item.title: New Startup Financing Program Launched in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan is launching new mechanisms to finance startups and attract private investors, as outlined in a presidential decree. The 'Entrepreneur of the Future' program will fund up to 30 startups by 2030 with investments up to 5 billion soms per project, focusing on priority sectors like IT and engineering.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Finance Ministry and EFSD Discuss Five-Year Cooperation Strategy
item.description: The Ministry of Finance of Kyrgyzstan and the Eurasian Fund for Stabilization and Development (EFSD) discussed key cooperation directions for the next five years. Representatives from the EFSD presented a draft of the fund's strategy for 2027–2031. The meeting focused on priorities for interaction with member states and potential areas for expanding financing programs in Kyrgyzstan's economy.

item.title: Uzbekistan Implements New Targeted Poverty Reduction System
item.description: Uzbekistan has reduced its poverty rate from 5.8% to 3.9%, lifting nearly 700,000 citizens out of need. A recent presidential meeting focused on poverty reduction and income growth, emphasizing that reforms must yield tangible results at the local level and improve citizens' daily lives and financial security.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank Sells $202.7 Million in Foreign Exchange Intervention
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan conducted a foreign exchange intervention on September 4, selling $202.7 million on the domestic market. This marks the eleventh intervention of the year and the second largest in volume. The central bank stated that such interventions are conducted to smooth out temporary imbalances between the demand and supply of foreign currency.

item.title: Russians unfit for military service may be involved in drone defense, Putin approves initiative
item.description: Individuals in Russia deemed unfit for military service may be offered contracts with the Ministry of Defense. They would not be sent to the front lines but would instead focus on protecting strategic sites within the country from drone threats.

item.title: EAEU countries to implement unified rules for marketplace goods returns
item.description: Unified rules for returning goods purchased from marketplaces will soon apply across Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) member states. An agreement on e-commerce, signed in August 2026, establishes common consumer protection standards for cross-border online purchases. Consumers will have a 14-day period to return quality goods, with provisions for dispute resolution and data security.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes fines for failure to report underage pregnancies or early marriages
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering imposing fines on individuals who fail to report underage pregnancies or early marriages to internal affairs bodies or "Inson" centers. This proposed legislation aims to hold accountable those obligated to report such violations but who neglect to do so, thereby addressing issues related to child marriage and teenage pregnancy.

item.title: Germany is priority destination for direct flights from Kyrgyzstan, says official
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering opening direct flights to Europe, with Germany as the priority destination, according to the head of the cabinet of ministers. Kyrgyzstan was removed from the EU's aviation safety blacklist in June. The country also aims to develop its startup and IT ecosystem.

item.title: Personnel Changes in Uzbekistan's Chamber of Accounts and Presidential Administration
item.description: Uzbekistan's Chamber of Accounts and Presidential Administration's Compliance Service have seen personnel changes. Two deputy heads of the Chamber of Accounts were appointed to new positions, and two other officials took deputy head roles. The changes were signed by the head of the Presidential Administration.

item.title: Three Kyrgyz enterprises gain export rights to European market
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Germany aim to strengthen business ties through the Kyrgyz-German Business Council. Discussions focused on supporting small and medium-sized businesses, developing winter tourism, and fostering the IT sector. Kyrgyzstan seeks to expand direct business contacts and promote its products in Germany, moving towards a value-added export chain.

item.title: Kremlin: Putin's talks with Trump envoys were substantive and confidential
item.description: The Kremlin described President Vladimir Putin's meetings with US special envoy Stephen Whitocoff and Jared Kushner as substantive, frank, and confidential. The talks, lasting over three hours, covered the situation in the conflict zone, Russian military successes, and potential US-Russia economic projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan's top 10 foreign trade partners revealed for first seven months
item.description: Uzbekistan has conducted trade with over 200 countries in the first seven months of the year. The National Statistics Committee has announced the country's top 10 foreign trade partners during this period.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Celebrates Independence Amidst SCO Summit and World Nomad Games
item.description: Kyrgyzstan marked its 35th Independence Day with a focus on the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek. The summit, chaired by President Sadyr Japarov, addressed regional security, economic ties, and transport corridors, resulting in the Bishkek Declaration. A new center to combat transnational organized crime will be established in Bishkek.

item.title: Putin Discusses Ukraine Settlement with Trump Envoys in Moscow
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Donald Trump's special envoy Stephen Witkoff and advisor Jared Kushner in Moscow to discuss the Ukrainian settlement. Putin stated that Russian forces had not struck Kyiv since September 5, and noted that Ukrainian forces had also reduced attacks on Russia. He expressed high trust in Witkoff and Kushner as mediators.

item.title: Uzbekistan Opens First Consulate in Seattle, USA, to Boost Bilateral Ties
item.description: Uzbekistan has officially opened its first consulate in the northwestern United States, located in Seattle. Presidential advisor Komil Allamjonov stated the consulate will further develop Uzbek-US relations, focusing on trade, investment, technology, education, and people-to-people exchanges.

item.title: Appointments Made at Accounts Chamber and Presidential Administration
item.description: New deputies have been appointed to the Accounts Chamber chairman's office, and a new head has been appointed to the compliance service department of the Presidential Administration, according to relevant orders from the administration head.
